subject: BankCorp: erasure TTL proofs & log delivery plan
messages:
From: Courtney Lane <courtney.lane@bankcorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: audits@bankcorp.com
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on erasure/TTL proof for SOC2 audit

Hi Rishi,

We're kicking off the BankCorp SOC2 readiness packet for our March audit window. A couple of quick asks we need from Redwood to satisfy our evidence list for retention/deletion controls:

1) A sampling of tenant-level erasure snapshots showing timeline (request timestamp, deletion job run timestamp, final tombstone confirmation) for 5 tenants we select.
2) Event log exports that prove TTL-triggered deletion events across Feb 1—Mar 7, including request IDs and worker IDs.
3) The runbook describing how TTL exceptions are handled and an example change-control entry for any TTL policy change in the last 12 months.

Can you confirm whether you can provide these items by Wed 10 Mar EOD PT? If not, tell us what you can do and by when — BankCorp needs evidence linked to retention/deletion for our auditor.

Thanks,
Courtney
Courtney Lane
Senior Information Security Manager
BankCorp Financial

[attachment: bankcorp-evidence-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Courtney Lane <courtney.lane@bankcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on erasure/TTL proof for SOC2 audit

Courtney — thanks for the clear list. We can meet the ask but will scope out what we can hand off as exported artifacts vs. guided access for sampling. High-level plan: 

- Erasure snapshots: we'll provide CSV snapshots for the 5 tenants you pick (same schema as our previous SOC2 handoffs: tenant_id, request_ts, job_start_ts, job_complete_ts, tombstone_confirm_ts). We will sanitize tenant identifiers with reversible hash salt per your preference.
- Event logs: we can export TTL-triggered events (ndjson) covering Feb 1—Mar 7 with request_id, action, worker_id, shard_id, and result. We will redact ephemeral worker IPs.
- Runbook & change control: attach the current deletion runbook (PDF) and an excerpt of our change-log showing the TTL policy change from 2026-11-12.

Deliverables and preliminary ETA:
- Wed 10 Mar 18:00 PT: erasure snapshots (CSV) + TTL event NDJSON sample + runbook PDF.
- If BankCorp needs additional forensic traces (S3 object manifests, manifest checksums), we can include them by Fri 12 Mar.

Please reply with the 5 tenant IDs (or allow us to pick a representative sampling from your tenant pool). Also confirm whether your auditor prefers salted IDs or full tenant IDs.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

[attachment: deletion-runbook-v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Questions on erasure/TTL proof for SOC2 audit

Rishi / Vivek — forwarding Courtney's ask. Quick internal notes below.

On Mon, 08 Mar 2027 at 11:00, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Courtney — thanks for the clear list. We can meet the ask but will scope out what we can hand off as exported artifacts vs. guided access for sampling. High-level plan: 
> ...

Internal checklist (to produce exports):
- Run the snapshot job for selected tenants (sys-admin-scripts/snapshots/run_snapshot.sh) — outputs to s3://redwood-evidence/erasure-snapshots/2027-03-08/.
- TTL event extraction query (kql): include request_id, action, worker_id, shard_id, result, and tz-normalized timestamps. Export as ndjson; limit PII fields.
- Prepare an attestation entry for auditor: short cover letter signed by me confirming the export method and the salt used for tenant hashing.

Vivek: can you schedule the snapshot job for Wed 10 Mar 02:00 PT (so we have working hours to validate) and stash outputs with the attestation header? Also need a short MD5 manifest for each CSV and NDJSON file.

Thanks — M.

Monica Patel
Senior Cloud Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Courtney Lane <courtney.lane@bankcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, audits@bankcorp.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on erasure/TTL proof for SOC2 audit — delivery

Courtney — delivering the artifacts per the plan. Files are attached and a Drive folder is shared below. Per your preference, tenant IDs are salted with the bank-supplied salt (we used the value you sent on Mar 8).

Summary of attachments delivered:
- redwood-erasure-snapshot-20270307.csv (5 tenant snapshots; columns: tenant_hash, request_ts, job_start_ts, job_complete_ts, tombstone_confirm_ts)
- ttl-event-log-20270201-20270307.ndjson (filtered TTL deletions; includes request_id, action, worker_id, shard_id, result)
- deletion-runbook-v2.pdf (current runbook)
- md5-manifest.txt (MD5 checksums for CSV/NDJSON)
- attestation-cover-letter-march10.pdf (signed attestation from Monica Patel)

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bErasureEvidence
HubSpot record: HubSpot-789654

Notes & caveats:
- We redacted ephemeral worker IPs and replaced tenant IDs with the salted hash value you approved. If the auditor requires raw tenant IDs, please confirm and we'll arrange a secure vault transfer under a mutual NDA.
- The NDJSON contains only TTL-triggered deletion events; GC/archival jobs are not included in that file. If you need the complete lifecycle trace (GC + archival + TTL), we can produce an expanded export by request.

Let us know if the auditor wants a short walkthrough call to validate the exports — happy to schedule a 30-minute session.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
